title: Over 782,000 S’poreans aged 50 & above to get up to S$1,500 CPF top-up by Dec. 8, no action needed

 Over 782,000 S’poreans aged 50 & above to get up to S$1,500 CPF top-up by Dec. 8, no action needed
 Top-up.
 Nyi Nyi Thet 
 November 20, 2026, 12:07 PM
Image from Google and Unsplash
 More than 782,000 eligible Singaporean seniors will receive a CPF top-up of up to S$1,500 by Dec. 8, the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) and the Central Provident Fund Board (CPFB) said in a joint press release on Nov. 20. 
 The top-up, first announced at Budget 2026, will cost S$1.04 billion in total. 
 It is meant to support seniors who may face challenges building their retirement savings, the agencies said. 
 Eligible recipients aged 55 and above will receive the top-up in their Retirement Account (RA), while those below 55 will get it in their Special Account (SA). 
 MOM and CPFB said the money will earn higher CPF interest rates in these accounts. 
 Who is eligible
 To qualify, a person must be a Singapore citizen residing in Singapore and born in 1976 or earlier. 
 They must have CPF retirement savings below the 2026 Basic Retirement Sum (BRS) of S$110,200 as at Dec. 31, 2025, and own no more than one property as at that date. 
 They must also live in a property with an Annual Value (AV) of not more than S$31,000 as at Dec. 31, 2025. 
 CPF retirement savings are based on the sum of a person’s RA and CPF LIFE balances. If the RA has not yet been created, they are based on the sum of the Ordinary Account (OA) and SA balances. 
 How much you will get
 The amount is tiered according to a person’s CPF retirement savings and the AV of their home. 
 Seniors whose homes have an AV of not more than S$21,000 will receive S$1,500 if their retirement savings are below S$60,000, and S$1,000 if their savings are at least S$60,000 but below S$110,200. 
 Those whose homes have an AV of more than S$21,000 but not more than S$31,000 will receive S$500, regardless of their savings, as long as they are below the S$110,200 threshold. 
 No action needed
 The top-up will be credited automatically, and recipients do not need to apply, MOM and CPFB said. More information is available at govbenefits.gov.sg . 
 Recipients will be notified by SMS via the gov.sg Sender ID after the top-up has been credited. 
 Those without a Singpass-registered mobile number will be informed by letter sent to their registered address on their Singapore identity card. 
 The agencies also reminded the public that government officials will never ask them to transfer money or disclose banking details over a phone call. Those who encounter possible scam calls or messages can call the ScamShield Helpline at 1799.
